record.paper_title: Open questions for strongly interacting Fermi gases with zero-range interactions
record.original_question: For a highly polarized two-component Fermi gas, determine the domain of existence, in the parameter space of polarization (N↑−N↓)/N, interaction strength 1/kFa, and reduced temperature T/TF, of a spatially modulated pair-condensed superfluid whose pairs occupy a superposition of nonzero center-of-mass plane-wave modes. The problem must account for sensitivity to thermal fluctuations and the absence of three-dimensional cold-atom experimental data.

evidence.quote: In the highly polarized case, where N↑ − N↓ is extensive like N , it is expected that T = 0 pair condensation may take place in a plane-wave superposition of their center of mass (rather than in Kpair = 0 as assumed here), see references [66, 67], giving rise to a spatially modulated superfluid (a supersolid following the fashionable terminology), with an imperfectly known domain of existence in parameter space (( N↑ − N↓)/N , 1/kFa,T /TF), the problem being complicated by its high sensitivity to thermal fluctuations [68] (there are as yet no experimental results in three-dimensional cold atom gases [69]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a three-dimensional two-component (spin-↑ and spin-↓) Fermi gas with zero-range s-wave interactions characterized by the scattering length a, at temperature T. Let N_↑ and N_↓ denote the number of fermions in each spin component, N = N_↑ + N_↓ the total number, k_F the Fermi wavenumber associated with the total density (via n = k_F^3/(3π^2) for the equivalent unpolarized gas), and T_F = ℏ^2 k_F^2/(2 m k_B) the Fermi temperature. Suppose the gas is highly polarized, i.e. N_↑ − N_↓ scales extensively with N.

It is conjectured that in such a system pair condensation can occur not at zero center-of-mass momentum K_pair = 0, but rather in a coherent superposition of plane-wave pair states with nonzero center-of-mass momenta, producing a spatially modulated pair-condensed superfluid (a "supersolid"-like phase, of FFLO type).

Problem: Determine, as precisely as possible, the domain of existence of this spatially modulated pair-condensed superfluid phase in the three-dimensional parameter space
  (p, 1/(k_F a), T/T_F),  with p = (N_↑ − N_↓)/N ∈ (0,1],
including the boundary of the domain. The determination must account for the high sensitivity of the modulated phase to thermal fluctuations.
artifact.category_tag: FFLO/supersolid phase in polarized Fermi gases
artifact.status_search_result: The FFLO/spatially-modulated superfluid phase has not been conclusively observed in 3D cold-atom experiments, and its precise domain of existence in (polarization, 1/k_F a, T/T_F) parameter space remains uncertain; theoretical predictions suggest only a narrow window in 3D, with strong sensitivity to thermal fluctuations. Searches in the 1D–3D crossover are ongoing but have not yielded a 3D phase boundary determination.

status_evidence.title: Search for the FFLO Phase in the 1D-3D Crossover of a Spin-Imbalanced Fermi Gas
status_evidence.snippet: Researchers confine spin-imbalanced 6Li to 1D tubes via a 2D optical lattice and tune toward the 3D regime to search for the elusive FFLO phase.
status_evidence.claim: The FFLO phase has not been conclusively observed in 3D cold-atom experiments and is being searched for in the 1D-3D crossover.

status_evidence.title: Ultra-cold Polarized Fermi Gases (Chevy & Mora)
status_evidence.snippet: Review discusses theoretical predictions for FFLO-type modulated superfluid phases in polarized Fermi gases and the narrow expected region in 3D.
status_evidence.claim: In 3D the FFLO modulated superfluid is believed to occupy only a small region of the phase diagram, with significant theoretical uncertainty.

status_evidence.title: Spin-Polarized Fermions in 1D and 3D — Hulet Lab
status_evidence.snippet: Experimental program studying spin-imbalanced Fermi gases; FFLO observed signatures in 1D but not confirmed in 3D.
status_evidence.claim: No definitive 3D experimental confirmation of the modulated superfluid phase exists.
